title: Locked Diary Predicts My Murder
captions: I found a locked diary that writes today’s date each morning. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #mystery #haunted
The diary just predicted a murder at my doorstep. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #thriller #prediction
Did I ignore fate or was it a prank? Verdict below! #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #debate #mystery
parts: [[ATTIC · 07:12 AM]] I found a locked diary in my attic that writes itself with today’s date every morning. [[RULE 1 · OPEN]] I pry it open with a rusted screwdriver. The cover creaks. Inside, a single page, ink fresh, reads: "July twenty‑four, nine thirteen PM – you die at your doorstep." My heart jumps. I stare at the page, at the exact time, at the words spelling my name. The attic smells of dust and old wood, a cold draft brushes my neck. I rush downstairs, the old floorboards groaning under my feet. [[DAY 1 · 07:30 AM]] I call my best friend, Maya, whispering, “It’s a joke, right?” She laughs, “Maybe you’re just tired.” I hang up, but the diary’s page flips by itself, a new line appearing: "If you ignore, the killer will wait.” I hear a faint ticking from the hallway clock. Panic spikes. I grab the diary, slam it shut, and bolt the attic door. [[3 MINUTES LEFT]] My phone buzzes – a text from an unknown number: “See you at nine‑thirteen.” I stare at the screen, breath shallow, eyes darting to the darkening sky. The sun slips behind clouds, shadows stretch. I hear a car idling outside, its engine humming like a warning. I glance at the clock – it reads eight fifty‑nine. I have eleven minutes. I swallow hard and step toward the front door, the diary heavy in my bag. [[CUT OFF BEFORE REVELATION]]

[[DAY 1 · 08:58 AM]] I’m still at the front door, the diary thudding against my chest. The car outside sputters, engine cooling. My hands shake, the knob cold under my fingers. I hear a soft knock, two rapid taps. I glance at the diary – the page is blank now, the ink faded. A new line forms: "He’ll knock twice, then step inside." My breath catches. I decide to open just a crack. The hallway light flickers, casting long shadows. [[RULE 2 · WAIT]] I count the knocks: one, two. I step back, heart pounding. A figure appears in the doorway, silhouette tall, coat soaked from rain. I can’t make out a face. "Who’s there?" I whisper, voice cracking. No answer, only the sound of rain hitting the porch. The diary flips again, ink spilling: "Don’t speak, he hears you.” I freeze, my throat dry. The stranger moves, hand reaching for the knob. I hear the clock tick: nine‑ten. My mind races. I think of Maya’s laugh, of the prank idea. Maybe it’s a friend trying to scare me. I glance at the diary, hoping for a clue. The page stays empty. The figure’s footsteps echo, each one louder. I hear a faint metallic click from inside the house – the front door lock disengaging. I realize I’m the only thing between him and the living room. [[9:11 PM · LIVING ROOM]] I grab the diary, fling it onto the couch, and slam the door shut, just as the knob turns. [[CUT OFF BEFORE REVELATION]]

[[DAY 1 · 09:13 PM]] The door bursts open, splintering wood, and a shadow lunges forward. I dodge, the diary slipping from my hands, pages fluttering like frantic birds. The intruder is a man in a dark hoodie, face hidden, eyes glinting. He lunges again, this time his hand gripping my wrist. I twist, hear the faint click of a hidden blade in his coat. I scramble backward, feeling the cold floorboards under my shoes. My breath is ragged, the attic diary now lying open on the couch, its last entry glowing: "He is you." I stare, horror dawning. The man steps back, pulls a small device from his pocket, and points it at me. "You wrote it," he snarls, voice distorted. "You invited me.” The clock on the wall ticks twelve seconds left. I realize the diary was never predicting – it was a trap I set for myself, a twisted game of self‑fulfilling prophecy. I grab a nearby lamp, swing it hard. The device sparks, a flash of light. The man staggers, drops the weapon, and collapses. I gasp, the diary’s pages fluttering, now blank. The front door slams shut on its own, wind howling through the cracks. I stand trembling, the house silent except for the ticking clock. I pick up the diary, its cover now cracked, the lock broken. Did I just survive because I believed the warning, or did I cause the murder to happen? So... was I wrong to trust a haunted diary, or was it all a cruel prank? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #verdict #mystery

premise.hook: I found a locked diary in my attic that writes itself with today's date every morning.
premise.twist: The diary predicts a murder that will happen at my doorstep at 9:13 PM, and the victim is me.
premise.debate: Viewers will argue if the narrator should trust a haunted diary and change fate, or if it’s a prank that could cause panic.
